title: それから — “and then / after that”
summary: それから links two sentences in time order: ‘After that, …’. It is used to describe actions in sequence, such as a daily routine, and can also add one more item to a list. It stands at the beginning of the next sentence.

patterns.gloss: Sentence 1. それから, sentence 2 (next in time)

body.p: それ means ‘that’ (the previous action) and から means ‘from’. Together it is ‘from that point on’: first A happened, then B.
It is perfect for talking about a day: 朝ご飯を食べました。それから学校へ行きました。You can chain it with a series: first, それから, 最後に.
てから joins two actions inside one sentence (食べてから行く). それから starts a new sentence. They express the same order, but それから is stand-alone and a bit more flexible.

examples.ja: 朝（あさ）ご飯（はん）を食（た）べました。それから学校（がっこう）へ行（い）きました。
examples.romaji: Asagohan o tabemashita. Sorekara gakkō e ikimashita.
examples.tr: I ate breakfast. After that, I went to school.

examples.ja: 顔（かお）を洗（あら）いました。それから歯（は）を磨（みが）きました。
examples.romaji: Kao o araimashita. Sorekara ha o migakimashita.
examples.tr: I washed my face. And then I brushed my teeth.

examples.ja: 買（か）い物（もの）をしました。それから家（いえ）に帰（かえ）りました。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o shimashita. Sorekara ie ni kaerimashita.
examples.tr: I went shopping. After that, I went home.
examples.note: Tense stays the same in both sentences.

pitfalls: それから is for things in order. To add an extra quality, use そして instead.
Don't confuse the sentence-starting それから with the in-sentence てから.
